title: Five Takeaways From Real Madrid’s Statement El Clasico Win That Exposed Barcelona
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 25, 2026Kylian Mbappé (middle) scored a brace to lead Real Madrid’s El Clásico victory.     / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty ImagesReal Madrid made a mockery of the pre-match predictions and deservedly defeated Barcelona 2–1 at the Camp Nou in the first El Clásico of the season.

The dominant Barcelona showing that many expected didn’t come to fruition, and Real Madrid were the superior side from the start in Sunday’s heavyweight bout. Los Blancos dictated terms and took the lead on the verge of halftime when Kylian Mbappé was at the right place at the right time, as Gerard Martín’s clumsy clearance hit the Frenchman and rebounded into the back of the net.

Although Barcelona improved in the second half and found an equalizer through Raphinha’s La Liga-leading 13th goal of the term from a fabulous Pedri assist, Hansi Flick’s side looked far from their best version.

When it seemed like El Clásico was destined to end in a draw, a brilliant run from Eduardo Camavinga allowed him to square Mbappé, who tapped in his match-winning 100th goal for Real Madrid in the 87th minute.

It was a statement performance from José Mourinho’s side. A deserved victory for a team that’s on the rise and a concerning defeat for Barcelona, who after starting the season looking like the best team in the world now look alarmingly beatable against strong opposition.
Here are five takeaways from the thrilling and unexpected result.

Jose Mourinho (middle) had his team ultra-prepared for El Clásico.  / Jose Hernandez/Anadolu/Getty ImagesReal Madrid played their best game of the season, and Mourinho deserves a huge amount of credit for how he set up his side and how incredibly prepared Los Blancos looked.

Those who expected Mourinho to revert to his old ways and “park the bus” at the Camp Nou were mistaken. Like Paris Saint-Germain midweek, Real Madrid were aggressive, often pressing Barcelona inside their own half, forcing mistakes.

Furthermore, Madrid man-marked Barcelona all over the pitch, with each player jumping to press relentlessly. When the hosts managed to sustain long possessions, Los Blancos dropped to a 4-1-4-1 mid-block, with Jude Bellingham tasked with putting pressure on Rodri, making it hard for the usually brilliant midfielder to pull the strings from deep.

The introduction of Bernardo Silva in midfield also hinted at Madrid’s attempt to have more control when in possession. The Portuguese star struggled at times out of possession, but on the ball, he was excellent. He reduced Aurélien Tchouaméni’s responsibilities in possession—the Frenchman was sensational as well—but was essential for Madrid’s clear attacking plan: pounce in transition. A perfect Silva long ball started the action of the opener following a passage of sustained possession from Los Blancos.

Real Madrid were significantly more intense than Barça from the start, outworking and outrunning the Catalans—a trademark of Mourinho’s vintage style. With an intelligent game plan and a tenacious attitude, El Clásico was played on Mourinho’s terms.
In his highly expected El Clásico return, Mourinho outclassed Flick and handed the German boss his first home defeat of the rivalry.

Kylian Mbappé is a different beast against Barcelona at the Camp Nou.  / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesThere’s no other way around it, Mbappé owns Barcelona. At the Camp Nou, the Frenchman is a guarantee of goals.
The opener might’ve been fortuitous and his winner a tap-in, but all goals count the same, and on the biggest stage when Los Blancos needed him most, Mbappé delivered—again.

Mbappé has now scored 14 goals against Barcelona thoughout his career and 11 of them have come at the Camp Nou. He has now scored eight goals in his first seven appearances in El Clásico, the joint-fastest it’s taken a player to reach eight goals in the bitter match-up.
The Frenchman now has two braces in five El Clásico appearances in La Liga, already more than what Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema accomplished in their careers.

In the past, Mbappé’s brilliance hadn’t sufficed for victory, seeing Los Blancos dominated by Barcelona in recent meetings. But on the night in which Real Madrid played their best El Clásico in recent memory, it was still Mbappé who made the biggest difference.

Marc Cucurella (left) got the better of Lamine Yamal. / Josep Lago/AFP/Getty Images“Im going to eat him alive,” was the phrase Yamal used to describe what he was going to do to Marc Cucurella in the fullback’s El Clásico debut. In the end, it was the curly-haired defender who ate Yamal up.

In one of the tastiest individual battles on the pitch, Cucurella imposed his will on Yamal like few left backs have been able to. From the moment the game started, the summer recruit stayed tight on Yamal and was physical in his marking, nudging him constantly and even roughing him up with fouls.
